proof: Each b_j is adjacent only to t,m,z among fixed colored vertices in the frozen family grammar.
With t=m=2 and z=1, both colors 3 and 4 are legal for every b_j.
There are no B-B edges and no A-B edges in G_{r,q}.
Therefore the q choices are independent and yield exactly 2^q restricted proper extensions.

normalization_effect: a1 and a2 are added to the seed with colors 3 and 4.
The unique pre-branch Y0 vertex z is adjacent to both a1 and a2.
Hence z ceases to be Y0 after seed-two; the frozen G_{r,q} branch has no other Y0 vertex.
Thus final residual Y0 is empty for every one of the 2^q B-color patterns.
The B-color choices do not alter seeded/list structure because B vertices are not adjacent to a1 or a2 and extension colors are not part of the normalized structural state unless precolored.

conservative_size_catalog.definition: Catalog canonical SIGMA states for q=1,...,N while retaining q as a multiplicity count rather than quotienting it away.

calibration.compression_statement: 2^q microscopic extension patterns collapse to one proof-interface state at each fixed q; retaining size/multiplicity across q<=N gives only N interface records.

CHAOS_B.reason: Within the frozen G_{2,q} calibration, making the unique Y0 vertex z survive seed-two while keeping both selected A vertices valid N(Y0) witnesses cannot be achieved by a single frozen-family edge mutation; no global absence claim is made.

CHAOS_C.reason: No distinct frozen source-legal normalization orders were bound for G_{2,q}; no confluence claim is made.

supported: Solution/extension multiplicity and proof-interface multiplicity are sharply different on an authoritative infinite family.
Zero entropy rate is not being used as the criterion; the conservative catalog itself is polynomial-size on this calibration.
This gives a concrete example of normalization suppressing proof-relevant branching.
not_supported: hardness or lower bounds from chaos metrics
